spec.name: Madreperla Piano Accordion
spec.description: A 36-key piano accordion with a 60-button bass side, set on the floor and shown in the Italian mother-of-pearl style: celluloid pearl swirls, black piano-lacquer bands, gold trim and a ruby bellows with cream-edged folds.
spec.layout:
STATIC MODEL, joints []. Real size, about 66 cm wide with the bellows half-open. It stands upright on the bottoms of its two cases on y=0, with the bellows axis along X and the front (+Z) facing the viewer. The player's right is world -X, so the TREBLE (piano keyboard) case is at -X and the BASS (button) case is at +X. Left to right in X: treble case [-0.33,-0.14], bellows [-0.14,0.14], bass case [0.14,0.318]. Both cases are 0.41 high and 0.22 deep (z -0.11..0.11). The bellows is smaller, y 0.02..0.39 and z -0.09..0.09, so the cases read as heavy ends with a ruby concertina between them. Front to back in Z: the keyboard and bellows strap stand proud of the front face (z up to 0.14 and 0.10), then the case fronts at z=0.11, then the case backs at z=-0.11, then the harness (straps and pads) from z=-0.11 to -0.17.

STYLE: every case surface is clad in mother-of-pearl celluloid. This is built as geometry, not paint. Each large face is a base slab in pearlWhite with several overlapping, slightly raised, irregular faceted pearl patches (thin extrudes or slabs 1-3 mm proud) in pearlPink, pearlAqua, pearlLilac, pearlCream and pearlShade, like swirled shell. A few small pearlHighlight flecks sit on top. Each face is framed by an inkBlack celluloid band about 6 mm wide, then a thin gold bead rail. Corners carry chrome caps and the underside has four black rubber feet 0.012 high. Rose and teal diamond inlays (roseInlay, tealInlay), repeated as one motif on the treble end face, the bass front panel and the bass-end panel border, tie the cases together. Bellows are ruby red with cream fold edges. All metal is gold or chrome. Every surface is a flat colour, and all detail is small parts seated on the surface.

parts.builds: The right-hand (treble) case WITHOUT the keys. A chamfered box shell with a pearlWhite base, x -0.33..-0.14, y 0..0.41, z -0.11..0.11. All faces except the bellows side get the pearl-swirl patchwork described in the layout. The OUTER END FACE (x=-0.33) is the show face: a big pearl swirl of 6-8 overlapping patches, a central rosette (a gold lathe ring around a pearlCream disc with 8 rose/teal diamond petals), and an inkBlack border with a gold bead rail. The FRONT FACE (z=0.11) shows pearl patches around the keyboard window x -0.32..-0.14, y 0.04..0.36 (left clear for the keyboard part), plus an inkBlack band above and below it and a gold rail round the window. The TOP FACE (y=0.41) carries a chrome slatted treble grille (about 12 thin chrome slats over a grilleDark recess, x -0.31..-0.17, z -0.06..0.06), a row of 7 register switches near the front top edge (pearlWhite tabs on chromeDark pivots, one gold master switch), a gold edge rail and pearl patches. The BACK FACE (z=-0.11) is a plainer pearl with an inkBlack leatherette strip and 2 chrome strap-anchor plates at the strap mounts. The inner face (x=-0.14) is a chrome bellows frame plate 0.006 thick with 8 screw heads. Four chrome corner caps on the vertical edges and 4 black rubber feet (0.012 high) under the corners at y 0..0.012.
parts.attaches: Inner face at x=-0.14 meets the bellows at trebleBellowsJoin. Front window is filled by the keyboard part starting at keyboardOrigin. Back anchor plates sit at shoulderStrapAnchorTreble and backTreble for the harness.

parts.builds: The piano keyboard on the treble front face, with the key axis along X and the notes stacked up Y. 21 white keys, each a keyIvory box 0.150 long (x -0.315..-0.165), about 0.0135 tall with 0.0012 gaps (pitch 0.0147 from y=0.046 to y=0.355), z 0.11..0.125, with a thin keyShade lower edge strip on each key and a rounded front lip. 15 black keys (inkBlack, 0.07 long at the outer end x -0.315..-0.245, 0.009 tall, z 0.11..0.135) sit on the boundary between white key i and i+1 (i counted from the bottom, i=0..19) when (i mod 7) is in {0,1,2,4,5}. Add a small pearlHighlight sheen strip on each black key. Behind the keys sits an inkBlack keybed backboard, x -0.32..-0.14, y 0.04..0.36, z 0.108..0.112. At the inner edge (x -0.165..-0.14) is a key-slip rail, a gold bar with a pearlCream inset and 3 tealInlay diamonds. At the top and bottom ends are pearl keyboard cheek blocks (pearlWhite, with pearlPink/pearlAqua swirl patches and a gold rail) 0.012 tall. A small gold brand plate (with a tiny engraved-look inkBlack line pattern or text) sits centred on the top cheek block.
parts.attaches: Backboard seats on the treble front face (z=0.11) at keyboardOrigin..keyboardTopEnd. Nothing protrudes past z=0.14.

parts.builds: The left-hand (bass) case, x 0.14..0.318, y 0..0.41, z -0.11..0.11, a chamfered pearlWhite shell with the same pearl-swirl patchwork, inkBlack bands, gold rails, chrome corner caps, 4 rubber feet and a chrome bellows frame plate at x=0.14. END PANEL at x=0.318 faces +X: an inkBlack recessed button board, y 0.04..0.38, z -0.095..0.095, bordered with a gold rail and rose/teal diamond inlays at the corners. On it sits a 6-column x 10-row grid of bass buttons. Column z = -0.075 + 0.03*c (c 0..5). Row y = 0.06 + 0.03*r (r 0..9), plus a stagger of c*0.006 in y. Each button is a short 8-sided pearl cylinder cap (0.0105 radius, 0.008 proud; pearlCream, with every third row inkBlack and every row 4 in roseInlay as root markers) on a gold ring collar (0.0125 radius, 0.003 high) with a tiny pearlHighlight dot on top. The tops of the buttons reach x=0.33. FRONT PANEL (z=0.11): a large pearl swirl plate framing a chrome slatted bass grille (about 9 vertical slats over grilleDark, x 0.17..0.29, y 0.08..0.33) with a gold oval brand badge centred above it. TOP: a chrome air-release button on a gold collar, plus a pearl patchwork and a gold edge rail. BACK: pearl with an inkBlack strip and a chrome strap-plate pair.
parts.attaches: Inner face x=0.14 meets the bellows at bassBellowsJoin. Back plates at handStrapPadBass, backBass and shoulderStrapAnchorBass for the harness. The bellows strap anchors at bellowsStrapAnchor (a gold stud on the bass front inner edge).

parts.builds: The ruby bellows between the two cases, x -0.14..0.14, outer y 0.02..0.39 and z -0.09..0.09 (half-open). 15 pleats, pitch about 0.0187 along X. Each pleat is a rectangular ridge ring (outer size 0.37 high x 0.17 deep) of 4 thin bellowsRed slabs, with angled flank panels in bellowsRedDark running down to inset valley rings (inset 0.012 on every side) between the ridges. Every ridge crest carries a thin bellowsEdge cream ring just proud of the red, the classic white fold edge. The four long corners of the bellows carry full-length corner guards, inkBlack L-profile strips with a gold centre bead and tiny gold studs every pleat, and a gold-and-pearl bellows frame lip at each end (x=-0.14 and x=0.14). A bellows strap on the front: a leather band 0.022 wide, lying at z 0.09..0.10 across the front of the bellows at y 0.2 from bellowsStrapAnchor toward x=-0.04, with stitch dashes in stitch, a gold buckle (frame, tongue and 2 rivets), 5 punched holes (inkBlack) and a loose end with a pointed tip and a pearlWhite keeper loop. A small gold bellows-valve plate sits on the top face at the centre pleat.
parts.attaches: Ends butt the case frame plates at trebleBellowsJoin (x=-0.14) and bassBellowsJoin (x=0.14). The strap root meets the bass case at bellowsStrapAnchor.

parts.builds: Everything on the BACK (z -0.11..-0.17): the player's straps. Two shoulder straps in leather, each a 0.03 wide flat band. The treble strap starts at shoulderStrapAnchorTreble with a chrome anchor loop and hangs down the back with a slight bow to z=-0.15, with a stitch seam in stitch along both edges, a chrome slider buckle with a prong at y=0.10, a padded cushion pad (a thick leather box with chamfered corners, 0.06 wide x 0.10 high x 0.02 thick, with a pearlShade piping line) at y 0.16..0.26, and a tail end near y=0.03 with a gold tip. The bass strap starts at shoulderStrapAnchorBass and mirrors the construction. A bass hand strap pad: at handStrapPadBass a leather panel 0.07 wide x 0.18 high x 0.012 thick on the bass back, with a vertical slot (grilleDark), stitch border, 4 gold rivets and a velvet-look inkBlack band. A pair of small chrome D-rings sit at the bottom back of each case, y 0.04. The back also carries a thin gold maker's plaque on each case-back (0.05 x 0.016, with 3 tiny inkBlack engraved-look lines). The straps seat flat against the back faces, with each strap root on its anchor plate.
parts.attaches: Seats on the case back faces (z=-0.11) at backTreble and backBass. Strap roots at shoulderStrapAnchorTreble and shoulderStrapAnchorBass; the hand pad at handStrapPadBass.

calls.reasoning:
I'm thinking through the design of a piano accordion with an Italian mother-of-pearl aesthetic — treble keyboard on the right, bellows in the center, bass buttons on the left, sized roughly 0.45m wide, 0.4m tall, and 0.2m deep as a static display piece.

I'm working out how it should be oriented so the keyboard side faces the viewer correctly, reasoning through the player's perspective to figure out which way the bellows axis and keyboard should face relative to the model's coordinate system.

I'm working out the keyboard orientation: treble keys run vertically on the right case's front face, while bass buttons sit on the left case, reachable by the player's left hand. I'll simplify by just going with the most common accordion layout for the model rather than overanalyzing the exact facing angles.

For the aesthetic, I'm picking a mother-of-pearl celluloid finish with iridescent whites, pinks, aqua, and lavender, accented by black piano-pearl inlay lines, gold or chrome fittings, and red bellows trimmed in white and gold.

Now I'm working out the proportions: right treble case around 0.20 wide by 0.42 high by 0.22 deep, bellows roughly 0.26 by 0.36 by 0.19, and the left bass case about 0.16 wide, while also thinking through how the accordion sits resting on its bottom edge.

I'm reasoning about the keyboard orientation on the treble side -- the keys are horizontal strips stacked vertically so pitch ascends from bottom to top, matching how a player would press them with the case resting upright.

Working out a reasonable approximation: roughly 21 white keys with 13 black keys interspersed in the standard 2-3 repeating pattern, giving 34 keys total. With a case height around 0.42, I'm sizing the keyboard region to about 0.30 tall, so each white key works out to roughly 0.0143 in height -- thin but workable for this scale.

I'm placing the keyboard on the front face around x [-0.30, -0.12], and thinking through where other accordion features belong — register switches on top of the right case, bass buttons on the left case's front-facing end, even though real accordion ergonomics are a bit more nuanced than this simplified layout.

Now I'm working out strap placement: bass buttons on the +X end face, a pearl grille on the bass case front, and the bass hand strap crossing the back. Shoulder straps attach as loops on the back and top of the treble case.

I'm settling on dimensions now—cases 0.40 tall standing on y=0, bellows 0.34 tall inset, with depths of 0.20 for each case and 0.17 for the folded bellows. Both cases rest on the floor with corner feet, while the bellows floats slightly above between y=0.03 and 0.37. I'm splitting the model into parts starting with the treble case: its shell, pearl cladding, and keys.

I'm fleshing out the rest of the part breakdown—treble case gets the keyboard with white and black keys, fascia, top grille, register switches, and pearl inlay; bass case gets the button grid, end plate, grille, strap, and mute; bellows gets the pleated folds, corner guards, gold stripes, and strap. I'm weighing whether to add a separate ornament/hardware group for the badge, straps, and feet, or fold those details into the existing three parts.

I'll simplify to 5 parts instead: treble case, a separate keyboard piece with keys and fascia, bass case, bellows, and harness. Now I'm working out the overall coordinate scheme—total width, height, and depth—so each box fits together proportionally.

I'm working out the keyboard key placement along the x-axis, figuring white versus black key extents and which side the black keys sit on relative to the bellows and player's fingers.

I'm trying to recall from accordion photos exactly which side the black keys sit relative to the player — whether they're nearer the bellows side or the outer edge, using the piano analogy of black keys sitting toward the back as a reference point.

Working that out, I settle on placing black keys toward the outer/rear end since fingertips reach from the bellows side, so I'm mapping out precise x and z coordinates for the key positions, fascia surround, and keybed, then starting to set the vertical range for the treble case keyboard area.

I'm figuring out the white key spacing for 21 keys across the treble range, then working out which boundaries between white keys get black keys, starting from F as the lowest note and tracking the standard pattern of gaps where no black key occurs (B-C and E-F).

This gives me 15 black keys to pair with the 21 white ones, totaling 36 keys. Now I'm sketching out the bass side dimensions, trying narrower symmetrical x-bounds to balance against the treble and bellows widths.

Settling on an overall accordion size of roughly [0.66, 0.40, 0.30], accounting for case height, carrying handle clearance, and the z-depth span from the back straps to the front keys.

I'm positioning the bass and treble cases symmetrically along the x-axis with the bellows centered between them, and sizing the bellows slightly smaller than the cases with around 13 pleats, along with defining the join points where the bellows attach to each case.

I'll keep joints empty since this is a static model, not something posable, and now I'm starting to define the color palette with pearl white and pearl pink tones.

Rounding out the palette with strap stitching, grille tones, button pearl accents, and rubber feet, landing around 21 colors total, then adding blush rose and teal accent hues for the iridescent swirl pattern across the pearl panels, black celluloid bands, and gold edging.

Now I'm budgeting parts across the model: roughly 170 for the treble case, 130 for the keyboard, 190 for the bass case with its button rows, 150 for the bellows, and 90 for the harness, totaling around 730 of the 900 limit. For the bellows I'm planning 15 pleats running along the length, each built as alternating wide outer ridges and narrower inner valleys.

Defining mount points next...

I'll keep the straps simple: flat bands hanging from the top-back anchors of each case, bowing slightly outward to z=-0.16 as they fall toward the floor, with the left strap from the bass case and right from the treble case.

The straps end at brass slider rings near the bottom, with a wider padded leather pad at mid-height. For the bellows strap itself, I'll place it as a leather band with a gold buckle running across the front, connecting from the bass case's front lower area toward the treble side.

I'll settle on the bellows strap as a leather band fixed to the bass case's front inner face, laying across the bellows front at z=0.09 and ending in a gold buckle plate with a pearl keeper loop. That resolves the harness details alongside the shoulder straps, bass hand strap with pad, and gold anchors.

I'm also thinking about the treble case details: register switches near the top front edge, a chrome-slatted grille for sound projection, and a pearl panel above the keyboard with a gold brand badge.

Working out the exact keyboard geometry now -- placing the white keys, keyslip edge, and keyboard box coordinates on the treble front face.

For the overall case shell, I'm planning to build it as a chamfered slab with gold bead trim rails around the front/back perimeter, a black celluloid rim band, and shallow pearl swirl inlays as flat overlapping slabs on the side panels, with a larger pearl swirl and lathe-turned gold rosette on the outer end face.

Now working out the bass side button panel: laying out the grid as roughly 6 columns across z by around 10-12 rows, each button built from a pearl cap cylinder plus a gold ring, budgeting the bass button count against the overall part limit.

I'm adding the air-release button near the top rear of the bass case, and tallying the part budget across tread case, keyboard, bass case, bellows, and harness to stay under 900 total. For the bellows, I'm estimating around 190 parts from the ridge rings, valley rings, and corner guards.

Now I'm working out the pleat geometry: 15 folds with a pitch of about 0.0187, ridge faces in bellows red with darker alternating flanks for shading, thin white edge rings at the crests, and gold-pearl corner guards with black bars and a gold center strip to mimic the classic bellows tape look. I'm also noting which elements sit on the floor versus float above it—the case floors are grounded, but the bellows and keyboard are offset upward.

Now I'm sorting out the harness straps, chrome/black stud feet under the cases, and the mount/joint list, then starting to draft the bounding boxes for parts like the treble case and keyboard, working out how their overlapping front edges affect the total depth dimension.

Adjusting the bass case width and button positions so they line up symmetrically with the treble case edges, keeping overall accordion width around 0.66-0.67, then starting the bellows box coordinates.
